column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
When a ray of light bounces off a polished surface, what can you say about the angles it makes and about the three lines involved?
Look at your reflection in a flat mirror and describe it: its size, its distance, its orientation and whether it can be caught on a screen.
How can you tell an inward-curved mirror from an outward-curved one by looking at its reflecting surface?
Name the point on the mirror, the point of the sphere it came from, the distance between them and the line joining them.
Parallel sunrays hit a concave mirror and a convex mirror. Describe what becomes of the reflected rays in each case.
If a mirror's sphere has a known radius, how do you get its focal length and where is the focus?
If you slide a candle slowly towards a concave mirror from far away, what keeps changing about its image?
Where must you hold your face relative to a concave mirror to see a bigger, upright image, and what happens to the image once you move further back past the focus?
Why would a torch, a dentist and a solar furnace all choose the same type of mirror?
Whatever distance you hold a pencil from a convex mirror, what kind of image do you get and where does it appear?
Why would a driver choose a curved-outward mirror over a flat one for watching the traffic behind?
How do you find where the image of one point of an object forms using just a couple of rays?
A ray travels straight towards the centre of the sphere the mirror was cut from. Where does it go after reflection and why?
Where do you start measuring distances for mirror problems, and on which side of the mirror does the object always sit?
For a real object in front of a mirror, what sign does its distance carry and why?
Which three distances does the mirror formula connect, and what must you keep consistent when you put numbers in?
A calculation gives a magnification of -2 for one mirror and +0.5 for another. What can you say about each image?
Why does a straw look broken where it enters a glass of water?
A ray passes in through one face of a glass block and out of the opposite parallel face. How does the leaving ray compare with the entering ray, and why?
Which three lines at a refracting surface always lie in one flat plane?
When you change the angle at which light hits the same two media, what stays the same and what do we call it?
If the refractive index of glass is 1.5, what does that tell you about how fast light goes in glass compared with air?
A ray goes from air into water. Does it speed up or slow down, and which way does it turn relative to the perpendicular at the surface?
Feel two magnifying glasses, one thick in the centre and one thin in the centre. What does each do to a beam of parallel light?
Where does sunlight go after passing through a convex lens, and how do you use that to estimate the lens's focal length?
Explain how a magnifying glass gets a bigger, upright view of a small insect and where the insect must be relative to the lens.
No matter how far or near you hold an object, what two things can you always say about the image a concave lens makes of it?
Which three rays are easiest to draw to find where a lens forms an image, and how does each behave?
When you substitute into a lens problem, from which point are all distances measured and which sign does each type of lens's focal length take?
Which three quantities does the lens formula connect, and how do you describe the size change an image has compared to the object?
Two lenses have focal lengths of 0.5 m and 2 m. Which one bends light more, and how would you express that as a number?
An optician prescribes a lens of power -3 D. What sort of lens is it, and what sort of lens would +3 D be?
